name: Web Application Security
tagline: The full web assessment stack: intercepting proxies, discovery, injection testing, API tooling, and OWASP-class vulnerability testing — nested by technique.

tools.name: Burp Suite
tools.desc: The de-facto intercepting proxy for manual testing: intercept/edit requests, inspect responses, map the app, and extend via a large BApp marketplace.
tools.when: Every manual web engagement; the default scratchpad for inspecting and shaping requests to an app you are authorized to test.

tools.name: OWASP ZAP
tools.desc: Free and open-source OWASP proxy with automated scanning, fuzzing, and a REST API for CI-driven baseline scanning.
tools.when: When you need a fully open, scriptable proxy with automated scanning you can drive from a pipeline against a staging app you own.

tools.name: Caido
tools.desc: Lightweight, modern intercepting proxy with a clean UI and fast request replay, built as a slim alternative to the heavyweight suites.
tools.when: When you want a quick, single-file proxy for interception and replay without a large install footprint.
tools.install: brew tap caido/caido && brew install caido

tools.name: ffuf
tools.desc: Extremely fast web fuzzer written in Go for directories, files, parameters, vhosts, and more; supports filters, recursion, and matchers.
tools.when: Anytime you need fast brute-force discovery of paths or parameters against a target you are authorized to test.

tools.name: gobuster
tools.desc: Simple multi-purpose fuzzer for directories, DNS subdomains, and virtual hosts using wordlists.
tools.when: When you want a lightweight, easy-to-script brute forcer without a big learning curve.

tools.name: feroxbuster
tools.desc: Fast, recursive content discovery fuzzer built in Rust that automatically scans discovered directories.
tools.when: When you want recursion and auto-re-scanning of found directories out of the box.

tools.name: dirsearch
tools.desc: Mature Python path scanner with threading, proxy support, and extensive filter/ignored-status options.
tools.when: When a simple, cross-platform Python scanner with many wordlist and output options is all you need.

tools.name: wfuzz
tools.desc: Flexible Python fuzzer for web content and parameter brute-forcing with rich payload/encoding options.
tools.when: When you need fine-grained iteration over multiple payload positions and encoding filters.

tools.name: sqlmap
tools.desc: The reference automated SQLi tool: detects and exploits injection in GET/POST/headers, enumerates DBMSes, and dumps data on targets you are authorized to test.
tools.when: When a parameter looks injectable and you want thorough detection plus DB fingerprinting, safe limits, and batch modes.

tools.name: NoSQLMap
tools.desc: Automated pentesting tool for NoSQL databases (MongoDB, CouchDB) injection and misconfiguration.
tools.when: When the backend is NoSQL and you need injection-point discovery against an app you own or have scope for.
tools.install: git clone https://github.com/codingo/NoSQLMap && pip3 install -r NoSQLMap/requirements.txt

tools.name: Commix
tools.desc: Automated OS command injection detection and exploitation with support for many injection techniques and filter bypasses.
tools.when: When you suspect command injection in a parameter or header and want an automated detector on authorized targets.
tools.install: git clone https://github.com/commixproject/commix && cd commix && python3 commix.py -h

tools.name: tplmap
tools.desc: Detects and exploits server-side template injection across engines (Jinja2, Twig, Freemarker, etc.).
tools.when: When an app renders user input inside templates and you need to confirm SSTI on a scope-authorized target.
tools.install: git clone https://github.com/epinna/tplmap && pip3 install -r tplmap/requirements.txt

tools.name: Dalfox
tools.desc: Fast, parameter-analysis XSS scanner written in Go with payload generation and Telegram/Discord notification support.
tools.when: When you want to automate XSS discovery against a list of endpoints on authorized targets and pipeline results.

tools.name: XSStrike
tools.desc: XSS detection suite with payload crafting, bruteforce, and WAF/filter-detection heuristics.
tools.when: When you need sophisticated payload crafting and WAF detection for manual XSS validation in your tests.
tools.install: git clone https://github.com/s0md3v/XSStrike && pip3 install -r XSStrike/requirements.txt

tools.name: mitmproxy
tools.desc: Interactive man-in-the-middle proxy with a powerful scriptable (Python) add-on API for request shaping and inspection.
tools.when: When you need programmatic control over intercepted API traffic (rewrite, capture, fuzz) in your tests.

tools.name: Postman
tools.desc: API client and collection runner for crafting, saving, and automating HTTP requests against services under test.
tools.when: When you need organized collections, environments, and simple automation to reason about an API's behavior.

tools.name: HTTPie
tools.desc: User-friendly command-line HTTP client with readable, colorful output for quick manual requests.
tools.when: For fast ad-hoc requests in a terminal during investigation without a heavyweight GUI.

tools.name: jwt_tool
tools.desc: Audits JSON Web Tokens: signature verification, algorithm confusion, and known CVE checks against tokens issued by apps you test.
tools.when: When an application uses JWTs and you need to inspect claims, check alg:none/confusion, and validate signing secrets.
tools.install: git clone https://github.com/ticarpi/jwt_tool && cd jwt_tool && python3 jwt_tool.py -h

tools.name: smuggler
tools.desc: Detects HTTP request smuggling variants (CL.TE, TE.CL, TE.TE obfuscation) against backend parsing mismatches.
tools.when: When a stack splits differently between proxies/back-ends and you want to test smuggling scenarios on authorized targets.
tools.install: git clone https://github.com/defparam/smuggler && python3 smuggler.py regex.txt urls.txt
